thread:
tara: Quick sync  we need to clarify quantized fallback behavior on model cards + provide a tiny SDK batch example. Customer support saw different behavior between hosted and private infra (fallback to fp32 vs rejecting). Can someone own a short doc + snippet?

min: I can take it. Plan: 1) add explicit compat note on each quantized variant (fallback behavior), 2) tiny JS + Py snippet showing safe batching with quant fallback, 3) a short FAQ blurb. ETA today.

felix: Add a line explaining runtime policy names: `strict` (reject), `fallback` (convert/route to fp32), `auto` (try quant then fallback). People get confused by the wording in current cards.

adeel: For private deployments, fallback may be disabled for cost/security reasons. Add a note that private customers should contact infra for an opt-in flag and include the CLI command.

min: Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1280 1  includes model-card captions, a short FAQ, and two SDK examples.

tara: For the JS snippet please show how to detect fallback in the response (metadata) so apps can log and alert on cost spikes.

min: Done. JS snippet:
```javascript
// send a batch and detect fallback
const resp = await client.generateBatch(batch);
if (resp.meta?.served_with === 'fp32') {
  logger.warn('fallback-to-fp32', { batch_size: batch.length });
}
```

felix: For Python include a small backoff example if strict policy rejects: retry with smaller batch or with `policy='fallback'`.

adeel: I'll paste the private-deploy CLI opt-in:
```
infra-cli feature enable --name quant-fallback --scope org:acme-corp
```

min: Added a micro-benchmark note: fallback to fp32 increases per-token cost ~2-3x and latency ~1.8x on our A100 baseline. Put the numbers as a single-line caution.

tara: Also add a short "how to test locally" snippet using the preview endpoint and the provided example-vecs.csv. That helps support triage.

min: Added test snippet and attached example-vecs.csv to the PR. Also added FAQ Q: "Why did my embedding/ generation request suddenly cost more?" A: "You triggered quant fallback due to incompatible kernel/seq/kv_cache; see model-card policy section."

felix: Quick review left two nits: clarify the `served_with` metadata field name and tighten the benchmark language.

min: fixed both and pushed.

tara: LGTM. Approving now. :white_check_mark:
